chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Wishing he had stayed an electrician
summary: Smith says he wishes he had stayed with electrical work in the 1920s and become a contractor.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: ...but I'm going to get rid of that thing next week.
Just sort of thinking back over your life, do you feel disappointed about what happened to your music? Do you feel it was all a waste of time?

Well, in a way. If I knew then what I know now, I wouldn't have went into it. I'd have stayed with what I was doing. I was working with fellows who was electricians, and we was wiring a lot of houses around... Ice houses, those old silver ice houses here...?
No. That was back in the 20's, before I started playing music for a living. And I wish many days I had stayed with it, because I'd have stayed home here, and today I might have had something.
When you say you might have had something, you mean you

Yeah. I might have had me some kind of little enterprise or something. I might have had some people working for me, have been a contractor. Because I'd have learned that electricity work, and I could have been finished years and years ago. And I wouldn't have had to be running all up and down the road everywhere. Most of the time I didn't have no job, just playing dance halls and running with all kinds of (?) and all kinds of folks, people, being abused, used and kicked around...
